Orders list: five orders.

Statement has five payments, each with txid matching order id. No duplicate e2e_id. No refunds lines.

So all payments can be linked to orders by txid.

Now evaluate status for each order.

We need to compare amount received vs order amount, and time relative to expires_at.

Also note rule 5: statuses order: unpaid, refunded, underpaid, overpaid, late_paid, paid. Use first that applies.

But also rule 9 says order of precedence: unpaid, refunded, underpaid, overpaid, late_paid, paid. So paid is last (requires exact amount and on time). Actually "late_paid" before "paid". So if payment exact amount but after expiry, then late_paid qualifies before paid.

Now compute per order.

1. PED-25601: order amount 972.84. Payment amount 972.84, time 2026-09-09T11:55:00-03:00. expires_at 12:15 -03:00. Payment is before expiry. Amount exact. So candidate statuses: underpaid? No. overpaid? No. late_paid? No (since before). paid? Yes. So status "paid". Payments list includes e2e_id "E4863589680002". No refunds.

2. PED-11514: amount 1208.95. Payment amount 1208.95 at 17:09, expires_at 17:15 -03:00. Payment before expiry (actually 6 minutes before). So exact amount on time -> paid. So status "paid". payment e2e_id "E7617271270005".

3. PED-34383: amount 1272.98. Payment same amount at 12:08, expires at 12:26. Before expiry, on time, exact amount => paid. status "paid". payment id "E8789076150004".

4. PED-83190: amount 1714.84. Payment same amount at 12:21, expires at 12:31. before expiry, exact => paid. status "paid". payment id "E2558273320001".

5. PED-31212: amount 794.79. Payment same amount at 10:09, expires at 10:33. before expiry, exact => paid. status "paid". payment id "E9993465400003".

No refunds, no over/under.

Now orphans: any payment lines not linked to any order. All linked, so no orphans. But rule 13: "orphans" contains payment lines only: a refund line is never an orphan. Since there are none, list is empty [].

Pay attention to sorting: payments list should be sorted. Single element, okay. Orphans sorted: empty list.

Now produce JSON:

{
 "orders": {
   "PED-83190": {"status":"paid","payments":["E2558273320001"]},
   "PED-25601": {"status":"paid","payments":["E4863589680002"]},
   "PED-31212": {"status":"paid","payments":["E9993465400003"]},
   "PED-34383": {"status":"paid","payments":["E8789076150004"]},
   "PED-11514": {"status":"paid","payments":["E7617271270005"]}
 },
 "orphans": []
}
